scenarios.name: healthy_range
scenarios.description: Entering 32.0 °C, leaving 29.0 °C — a 3.0 K range, inside the 2.2-3.2 K healthy p50 band the 4-climate simulation study found, with the fan modulating at 60%. Evaluated and silent.

scenarios.name: range_collapsed
scenarios.description: Entering 30.0 °C, leaving 29.2 °C — a 0.8 K range against the 1.0 K band, with the fan at 60%. The alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay because delayOnInit holds the condition from the first tick.

scenarios.name: fan_below_eval_floor
scenarios.description: The same collapsed 0.8 K range with the fan idling at 20%. A tower whose fan is barely turning rejects little heat and its range says nothing about the condenser loop, which is what yFanOk = false tells the host: NO_EVAL, not a healthy tower.

scenarios.name: range_exactly_at_the_band
scenarios.description: Boundary, bit-exact: 30.0 − 29.0 is exactly 1.0 in IEEE-754 and range_low_band is exactly 1.0. Reals.LessThreshold is strict, so exactly-on-the-band reads healthy.

scenarios.name: range_just_below_the_band
scenarios.description: Boundary from below: 30.0 − 29.01 = 0.99 K clears the strict comparison by 10 mK and alarms on the normal schedule.

scenarios.name: range_just_above_the_band
scenarios.description: Boundary from above: 30.0 − 28.99 = 1.01 K never alarms, however marginal the loop is. Ten milli-kelvin is an order of magnitude inside any condenser-water sensor's error, which is the point of the placeholder warning on the band.

scenarios.name: fan_speed_exactly_at_the_floor
scenarios.description: Boundary on the other conjunct: the fan sits at exactly min_fan_speed_for_eval (30%) with the range collapsed. Reals.GreaterThreshold is strict, so exactly-at-the-floor is NO_EVAL and the rule stays silent.

scenarios.name: fan_speed_just_above_the_floor
scenarios.description: 30.1% with the same collapsed range: evaluable, and the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay. One tenth of a percent of fan speed is the whole difference between this scenario and the previous one.

scenarios.name: range_collapses_mid_run
scenarios.description: A tower holding a healthy 3.0 K range loses it at t = 1800 s — a second condenser pump starting, or a bypass valve opening. The alarm lands at exactly 5400 s: the mid-run rising edge carries the same T + delayTime arithmetic as the init case.

scenarios.name: range_recovers_after_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 3600 s and the range comes back at t = 5400 s when the extra pump stops. TrueDelay passes the falling edge with no delay, so yFault drops on that tick.

scenarios.name: fan_slows_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The evaluability release: an alarming tower drops to 15% fan at t = 5400 s with the collapsed range unchanged. yFault and yFanOk fall on the same tick, and only the pair tells the host that the tower unloaded rather than that the range recovered.

scenarios.name: intermittent_collapse_never_alarms
scenarios.description: Range alternating between 0.8 K and 3.0 K every 1200 s — a condenser pump staging on and off, or a chiller cycling. No single episode reaches alarm_delay, so nothing fires. Persistence is not averaging: a loop spending half its day at 0.8 K range is a real finding this rule cannot make.

scenarios.name: loop_side_semantics_inverted
scenarios.description: Blind spot, pinned: the two water sensors are bound the wrong way round (entering 29.0 °C, leaving 32.0 °C), so range reads −3.0 K. Nothing in the graph knows a negative range is impossible, and the rule reports the strongest possible collapse on a tower that may be running perfectly. The tower dictionary's loop-side note is the check: leaving is the COLD side.
